title: Multilang interop regression harness
summary: Working doc for a lightweight harness to catch regression signals that only surface in mixed-script inputs and locale-sensitive outputs. Focus on interoperability between prompt templates, model tokenization quirks, and downstream formatting (dates, numbers, currency, RTL embedding).
purpose: Create a repeatable eval harness that highlights regressions introduced by model changes, quantization, or tokenizer updates where conventional BLEU/ROUGE misses user-facing failures (e.g., wrong currency symbol reorder, RTL mark insertion in mixed CJK+RTL strings, numeric punctuation swapped).
background: We onboarded several open models recently and observed intermittent bugs: 1) models dropping ZWNJ or inserting LRM around Arabic substrings inside Chinese sentences; 2) decimal/thousand separator flip depending on seed/quant; 3) paraphrase-preserving meaning shifts in date normalization. Existing evals focus on translation-quality in isolation — this harness targets mixed-context failures that break UI pipelines.
scope: Targeted probes (small prompt sets) rather than full-scale eval suites. Goal: fast feedback (<30s per model on CI) and high precision for engineering triage. Not intended to replace larger eval corpora, but to act as a canary for regressions affecting locale formatting and mixed-script integrity.
scenarios: CJK sentence with embedded RTL phrase (Arabic/Hebrew) — verify bidi markers and glyph ordering preserved
RTL sentence with embedded English technical term and numbers — check LTR/RTL span preservation
Translation roundtrip (en -> zh -> en) for short UI strings containing dates and currency — detect formatting drift
Locale-aware numeric formatting: 1,234.56 vs 1.234,56 vs 1 234,56 — ensure output uses target locale conventions
Currency placement and symbol normalization across locales: "USD 1,200" vs "1.200,00 ${symbol}"
Tokenization edge: mixed script emoji + CJK + Arabic — detect dropped or merged tokens that impact meaning
prompt_examples: [EN->ZH] Translate UI label: "Last updated: 2026-03-01 14:05 (UTC)" — preserve date format for zh-CN convention or provide ISO if requested
[ZH+AR mix] 用户可在此处输入评论: "فعلا ممتاز" — return a single string suitable for display without inserting directional marks
[AR->EN] Convert "٠١/٠٢/٢٠٢٦" to ISO date and clarify ambiguity if any
[EN->FR] Format currency: "$1,234.50" into fr-FR local display
[EN roundtrip] Short phrase with parentheses and abbreviations: "ETA (approx.) 3:30pm" — ensure punctuation preserved
evaluation_metrics: locale-match-rate: fraction of outputs that use expected decimal/thousand separators for target locale
currency-placement-accuracy: exact match on symbol position and spacing
bidi-integrity: presence/absence of explicit RTL/LTR markers relative to baseline and rendering-safe ordering
numeric-f1: fuzzy numeric match tolerant to formatting but strict on magnitude and precision
semantic-stability-score: embedding-similarity based check to detect meaning flips beyond simple token edits
tokenization-delta: heuristic count of token boundary changes vs baseline tokenizer for mixed-script inputs
harness_instructions: Run the harness as part of model onboarding CI or nightly regression. The test set is intentionally small (~250 prompts) to keep runtime quick. Each prompt is paired with a target locale, an expected normalization profile, and a tolerance rule. Failures should open a triage issue tagged 'aml/interop' with model id and seed. Prioritize failures that affect rendering (currency, date, bidi) over stylistic differences.
expected_artifacts: results/<model-id>.csv — raw outputs and per-prompt diagnostics
artifacts/stable/interop-baseline.csv — committed baseline for regression comparisons
known_issues: Some large-context models will canonicalize dates to verbose English irrespective of requested locale — acceptable for canary if numeric and month are preserved
Quantized variants occasionally drop combining marks in Arabic when sequence length > 256 — high false positive rate, add tolerance for combining-mark-loss within specified thresholds
Tokenization-delta currently flags changes aggressively when new tokenizer merges emoji sequences; we need whitelist rules
open_questions: What threshold for semantic-stability-score should trigger a P0 triage? Suggest start at cosine < 0.82 vs baseline embeddings.
Should the harness attempt to post-process expected outputs with ICUs to tolerate acceptable formatting differences, or keep expectations strict?
Who owns the baseline artifact updates when a legitimate improvement changes canonical outputs? Proposal: Model owner + eng-applied-ml sign-off in PR.
notes_to_self: Next steps: (1) synthesize 50 more mixed-script prompts targeted at product strings (settings, invoices), (2) add screenshot-based render checks for bidi in Storybook, (3) wire a GitHub action to auto-open triage issues with first-failure stack and minimal reproduction. Add review with UX for acceptable formatting drift.
